description: We are May the Pulse Be With You, a team of Electrical and Computer Engineers passionate about space exploration, technology, and astronaut health. We bring curiosity, creativity, and a little inspiration from a galaxy far, far away.
summary:
PULSE is a health monitoring app for astronauts on long-duration missions, such as a journey to Mars. It brings each crew member’s daily check-ins, symptoms, exercise, medicines and emotional wellbeing together with the cabin’s air and radiation data in one place. It is designed to be incredibly easy for anyone to use: it gives daily reminders, such as when a dose is due, and shows exactly where to find medicines and equipment in an emergency.
For the Health monitoring software challenge, PULSE helps the crew watch their own health and act on it on board. Far from Earth, messages take minutes to arrive, so the crew can’t count on doctors on the ground in the moment. With PULSE, the onboard medical officer approves medicines and any crew member can unlock emergency supplies straight away. Doctors on Earth still receive health reports and approve controlled medicines despite the delay. A calm, simple tool like this lowers everyday stress and helps the crew stay healthy on long missions.
details:
PULSE aims to be a hub for wellbeing and an everyday tool for astronauts on long-duration space missions. It is an app built around health monitoring, fitness and emotional wellbeing. Its main benefit is the range of its features, from exercise monitoring to an on-board companion for emotional check-ins and support, while everything stays clean and easy to use.

Astronauts log a daily check-in and can report a symptom by pointing to where it hurts on an interactive 3D body. The app compares each check-in with that person’s own history. The cabin screen shows CO₂, temperature, humidity and radiation from archived NASA mission data, and warns when a value leaves safe limits. Some medicines can be taken directly as self-care. Others need the onboard medical officer’s approval, and controlled medicines need approval from Earth, which arrives after the communication delay as a code or QR. Allergies are checked before any medicine is given. In an emergency, any crew member can unlock emergency medicines and equipment for a crewmate straight away. Each astronaut also keeps a private journal that only they can read, and the medical officer can send health reports to doctors on Earth. Healthy routines earn Pulsars, small rewards that unlock new looks for the companion. The opening screen is a star map that shows how far the crew is from Earth.

The intended impact is to reduce the stress of everyday life in space. The app reminds astronauts about their health, for example when a dose is due, and shows them where to find a medicine when they need it.

PULSE is coded in JavaScript. It runs on a Node.js 24 server with no external packages, and its browser pages use HTML and CSS. The interactive 3D body uses the three.js library. The app runs in a web browser, a camera can scan the QR codes from Earth, and the team worked together on GitHub. The demo uses fictional crew members and archived NASA measurements; no live sensors are connected yet.

[New: creativity] PULSE joins things that usually live in separate tools. The medical officer’s report puts a crew member’s symptoms next to their sleep, allergies, medicines and the cabin conditions at the time. Earth’s slow replies are part of the design rather than ignored: approvals arrive as codes or QR codes the crew can scan. A friendly mascot companion, a pixel-art star map and Pulsars rewards make daily health routines feel lighter.
